title: Extension by an essentially constant system preserves Mittag-Leffler (Stacks 070D)
statement: Let $0\to(A_i)\to(B_i)\to(C_i)\to0$ be a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by $i\ge1$ [def-weil-inverse-system] (morphisms of inverse systems $(A_i)\to(B_i)\to(C_i)$ such that $0\to A_i\to B_i\to C_i\to0$ is exact for every $i$). If $(C_i)$ is essentially constant [def-weil-pbc-essentially-constant-system], then $(A_i)$ is ML if and only if $(B_i)$ is ML [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system].

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 070D (lemma-exact-sequence-ML, homology.tex line 7761), with its proof lines 7771--7807 (uses Lemma 070C, lemma-essentially-constant, line 7733). Tags verified in tags/tags: 070D,homology-lemma-exact-sequence-ML; 070C,homology-lemma-essentially-constant

proof.text: Notation and dropping the first indices. Write $u_i:A_i\to B_i$, $v_i:B_i\to C_i$ for the maps of the sequence and $a_{k,i},b_{k,i},t_{k,i}$ ($k\ge i$) for the composite transition maps of $(A_i),(B_i),(C_i)$; since $u_i$ is injective and $u_ia_{k,i}=b_{k,i}u_k$, we identify $A_i$ with the subgroup $u_i(A_i)=\ker v_i$ of $B_i$, and then $a_{k,i}$ is the restriction of $b_{k,i}$ and $\operatorname{Im}(A_k\to A_i)=b_{k,i}(A_k)$. For $N\ge1$, an inverse system $(M_i)_{i\ge N}$ is called ML if the system $(M_{N-1+n})_{n\ge1}$ is ML [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system], i.e. for every $i\ge N$ there is $c(i)\ge i$ with $\operatorname{Im}(M_k\to M_i)=\operatorname{Im}(M_{c(i)}\to M_i)$ for all $k\ge c(i)$. Claim: $(M_i)_{i\ge1}$ is ML iff $(M_i)_{i\ge N}$ is ML. If $(M_i)_{i\ge1}$ is ML, its $c(i)$ for $i\ge N$ work. Conversely, given $c(i)$ for $i\ge N$, put $c(i)=c(N)$ for $i<N$ (so $c(i)\ge N>i$): for $k\ge c(N)$, $\operatorname{Im}(M_k\to M_i)=m_{N,i}(\operatorname{Im}(M_k\to M_N))=m_{N,i}(\operatorname{Im}(M_{c(N)}\to M_N))=\operatorname{Im}(M_{c(N)}\to M_i)$, where $m_{N,i}$ is the transition map and the composites factor through $M_N$. So it suffices to prove: $(A_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML iff $(B_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML, with $i_0$ the index of Step 2. (This is the source's 'after renumbering'.)

source.place: Homology, proof of Lemma 070D, line 7772 ('After renumbering')

proof.text: The decomposition of $(C_i)$. Since $(C_i)$ is essentially constant [def-weil-pbc-essentially-constant-system], choose $X$, $\pi_i:X\to C_i$, $i_0$ and $r:C_{i_0}\to X$ as in that definition, and for $j\ge i_0$ let $p_j=r\circ t_{j,i_0}$ and $Z_j=\ker p_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-essentially-constant-splitting]: (1) $p_j\pi_j=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $C_j=\pi_j(X)\oplus Z_j$; (2) $t_{k,j}\pi_k=\pi_j$ and $p_jt_{k,j}=p_k$ for $k\ge j\ge i_0$, so $(Z_j)_{j\ge i_0}$ is an inverse system under the restrictions $z_{k,j}$ of $t_{k,j}$; (3) for every $j\ge i_0$ there is $j^*\ge j$ with $z_{j^*,j}=0$. Let $q_j:C_j\to Z_j$, $q_j(c)=c-\pi_jp_j(c)$, be the projection along $\pi_j(X)$: it lands in $Z_j$ since $p_j(c-\pi_jp_jc)=p_jc-p_jc=0$ by (1), it is surjective (identity on $Z_j$), and $\ker q_j=\pi_j(X)$ by (1). It commutes with the transition maps: $q_j(t_{k,j}c)=t_{k,j}c-\pi_jp_jt_{k,j}c=t_{k,j}c-\pi_jp_kc=t_{k,j}c-t_{k,j}\pi_kp_kc=t_{k,j}(q_kc)$ by (2). (This is the source's $C_i=C\oplus Z_i$, with $C=X$.)

The case of an essentially zero quotient: the inclusions of images. Let $N\ge1$ and let $0\to(A'_i)\to(B'_i)\xrightarrow{w}(Z'_i)\to0$ be a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by $i\ge N$ [def-weil-inverse-system], with $A'_i=\ker w_i\subseteq B'_i$ as in Step 1 (transition maps $b'_{k,i}$, restricting to those of $(A'_i)$), such that for every $m\ge N$ there is $m^*\ge m$ with $Z'_{m^*}\to Z'_m$ zero. Then $b'_{m^*,m}(B'_{m^*})\subseteq A'_m$, because $w_m\circ b'_{m^*,m}=(Z'_{m^*}\to Z'_m)\circ w_{m^*}=0$. Hence for $N\le i\le m$ and $k\ge m^*$: $\operatorname{Im}(A'_k\to A'_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(B'_k\to B'_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(A'_m\to A'_i)$ $(*)$: the first since $A'_k\subseteq B'_k$ and $b'_{k,i}$ restricts to the transition map of $(A'_i)$; the second since $b'_{k,i}=b'_{m,i}\circ b'_{m^*,m}\circ b'_{k,m^*}$, so $b'_{k,i}(B'_k)\subseteq b'_{m,i}(A'_m)=\operatorname{Im}(A'_m\to A'_i)$. (This is the source's chain $\operatorname{Im}(A_{n_j}\to A_{n_i})\subset\operatorname{Im}(B_{n_j}\to B_{n_i})\subset\operatorname{Im}(A_{n_{j-1}}\to A_{n_i})$, with an arbitrary intermediate index $m$ in place of a subsequence $n_j$.)

source.place: Homology, proof of Lemma 070D, lines 7779--7787 (the case C = 0)

proof.text: The case of an essentially zero quotient: the equivalence. In the situation of Step 3, $(A'_i)_{i\ge N}$ is ML iff $(B'_i)_{i\ge N}$ is ML [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]. Fix $i\ge N$. If $(A'_i)$ is ML, let $c=c_{A'}(i)\ge i$ and $c'=c^*\ge c$ (Step 3 with $m=c$). For $k\ge c'$, $(*)$ with $m=c$ gives $\operatorname{Im}(A'_k\to A'_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(B'_k\to B'_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(A'_c\to A'_i)=\operatorname{Im}(A'_k\to A'_i)$, so $\operatorname{Im}(B'_k\to B'_i)=\operatorname{Im}(A'_c\to A'_i)$ for all $k\ge c'$; thus $c_{B'}(i)=c'$ works. If $(B'_i)$ is ML, let $c=c_{B'}(i)\ge i$. For $k\ge c$, $(*)$ with $m=k$ and the index $k^*\ge k$ gives $\operatorname{Im}(B'_{k^*}\to B'_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(A'_k\to A'_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(B'_k\to B'_i)$, and both outer groups equal $\operatorname{Im}(B'_c\to B'_i)$ since $k^*\ge k\ge c$; so $\operatorname{Im}(A'_k\to A'_i)=\operatorname{Im}(B'_c\to B'_i)$ for all $k\ge c$, and $c_{A'}(i)=c$ works. (This writes out the source's 'small detail omitted'.)

source.place: Homology, proof of Lemma 070D, lines 7788--7790 ('The equivalence follows from this (small detail omitted)')

proof.text: Replacing $(B_i)$ by the preimage of $X$. For $i\ge i_0$ let $B'_i=v_i^{-1}(\pi_i(X))\subseteq B_i$. For $k\ge i\ge i_0$, $b_{k,i}(B'_k)\subseteq B'_i$, since $v_ib_{k,i}=t_{k,i}v_k$ and $t_{k,i}\pi_k=\pi_i$ (Step 2 (2)); so $(B'_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] under the restricted maps. Let $w_i=q_i\circ v_i:B_i\to Z_i$ ($q_i$ of Step 2). It is surjective ($v_i$ and $q_i$ are), its kernel is $v_i^{-1}(\ker q_i)=v_i^{-1}(\pi_i(X))=B'_i$, and $w_ib_{k,i}=q_it_{k,i}v_k=z_{k,i}q_kv_k=z_{k,i}w_k$ (Step 2). So $0\to(B'_i)\to(B_i)_{i\ge i_0}\xrightarrow{w}(Z_i)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of inverse systems indexed by $i\ge i_0$, and $(Z_i)$ satisfies the hypothesis of Step 3 by Step 2 (3). By Steps 3 and 4 (with $N=i_0$, $A'=B'$, $B'=B$, $Z'=Z$): $(B'_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML iff $(B_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML.

The sequence $0\to A_i\to B'_i\to X\to0$. For $i\ge i_0$ let $s_i=p_i\circ v_i|_{B'_i}:B'_i\to X$. Then $A_i=\ker v_i\subseteq B'_i$, and $0\to A_i\to B'_i\xrightarrow{s_i}X\to0$ is exact: if $b\in B'_i$ and $s_i(b)=0$, then $v_i(b)\in\pi_i(X)\cap Z_i=0$ (Step 2 (1)), so $b\in A_i$; conversely $s_i(A_i)=0$; for $x\in X$ choose $b\in B_i$ with $v_i(b)=\pi_i(x)$ ($v_i$ is surjective), then $b\in B'_i$ and $s_i(b)=p_i\pi_i(x)=x$. The maps $s_i$ are compatible with the transition maps and the identity of $X$: $s_ib_{k,i}=p_iv_ib_{k,i}=p_it_{k,i}v_k=p_kv_k=s_k$ on $B'_k$ (Step 2 (2)). (The source's 'exact sequences $0\to A_i\to B_i\to C\to0$ for all $i$' after replacing $B$ by $B'$.)

The images form short exact sequences. For $k\ge i\ge i_0$ put $I_{k,i}=\operatorname{Im}(A_k\to A_i)=b_{k,i}(A_k)$ and $J_{k,i}=\operatorname{Im}(B'_k\to B'_i)=b_{k,i}(B'_k)$. Then $I_{k,i}\subseteq J_{k,i}$, (i) $s_i(J_{k,i})=X$, since $s_i\circ b_{k,i}=s_k$ is surjective (Step 6), and (ii) $J_{k,i}\cap A_i=I_{k,i}$: if $y=b_{k,i}(b)\in A_i$ with $b\in B'_k$, then $s_k(b)=s_i(y)=0$, so $b\in A_k$ and $y\in I_{k,i}$. That is, $0\to I_{k,i}\to J_{k,i}\xrightarrow{s_i}X\to0$ is exact.

Stabilization. $(A_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML iff $(B'_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]. Fix $i\ge i_0$; for $k\ge c\ge i$ we have $J_{k,i}\subseteq J_{c,i}$ and $I_{k,i}\subseteq I_{c,i}$, since $b_{k,i}=b_{c,i}\circ b_{k,c}$. If $(A_i)$ is ML with $c=c_A(i)$, let $k\ge c$ and $y\in J_{c,i}$: by Step 7 (i) choose $y'\in J_{k,i}$ with $s_i(y')=s_i(y)$; then $y-y'\in A_i\cap J_{c,i}=I_{c,i}=I_{k,i}\subseteq J_{k,i}$ (Step 7 (ii)), so $y\in J_{k,i}$. Hence $J_{k,i}=J_{c,i}$ for all $k\ge c$, and $c_{B'}(i)=c$ works. If $(B'_i)$ is ML with $c=c_{B'}(i)$, then for $k\ge c$, $I_{k,i}=J_{k,i}\cap A_i=J_{c,i}\cap A_i=I_{c,i}$ by Step 7 (ii), and $c_A(i)=c$ works.
Conclusion. By Step 1, $(A_i)$ is ML iff $(A_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML; by Step 8 this holds iff $(B'_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML; by Step 5 iff $(B_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is ML; by Step 1 iff $(B_i)$ is ML.
